title: Postcard and Songbook
premise: Juniper Joubert's failing café joins a town-run anonymous pen-pal program meant to pair lonely strangers; instead, a clerical error pairs her with Theo Marchand, the developer whose demolition notice threatens her block — and who once broke her heart in culinary school. Their letters, unaware at first of each other's identity, become the honest conversation they never managed face-to-face, even as Juniper organizes an off-the-books campaign to save the café block and Theo wrestles with evidence that his firm's eviction records were falsified. When identities are revealed mid-correspondence, both must choose between pride and truth: Theo testifies against his own company, and Juniper risks the whole heart instead of lending pieces. The café is saved by a community land trust, and the two meet at last as themselves, postcards no longer needed.
about_author: Ivo Brightwater is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, courtrooms, and small towns with long memories. They live near the coast, where they collect postcards from strangers and answer every one.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She counts the café's remaining weeks while frosting a wedding cake she can't afford to fail on, establishing her rule: love stays in past tense. Emotional beat: weary defiance masking fear.

chapters.title: The Pen-Pal Box
chapters.summary: The librarian launches the town's anonymous letter program to fight winter loneliness; Juniper signs up on a dare from her barista, Priya. POV: Juniper. Beat: cautious hope entering a closed heart.

chapters.title: Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He arrives in Bellhaven representing Marchand Development, posting eviction notices on the very block containing Juniper's café — though he doesn't yet know it's hers. Beat: dutiful unease.

chapters.title: First Letter, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Juniper writes about grief and burnt sugar; her correspondent answers with startling honesty about complicity and regret. Neither knows the other's name. Alternating letters, Juniper's framing POV. Beat: unexpected intimacy.

chapters.title: Flour and Antagonists
chapters.summary: In person, Juniper confronts Theo at a town meeting and recognizes him — the man who plagiarized her final pastry portfolio years ago. She storms out; he doesn't know why she hates him. POV alternates. Beat: old wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Correspondent Confides
chapters.summary: Theo, unaware his pen pal is Juniper, confesses to his anonymous friend that he stole work once, desperate and broke, and has regretted it ever since. POV: Theo. Beat: guilt seeking absolution.

chapters.title: A Recipe for Resistance
chapters.summary: Juniper channels anger into organizing: a night market fundraiser, petitions, an archive of the block's history. Priya worries she's fighting the building, not the feeling. POV: Juniper. Beat: purpose displacing pain.

chapters.title: Postcard from the Past
chapters.summary: Juniper finds an old culinary-school postcard in Theo's public file — proof he kept her recipe card all these years. She says nothing, but it unsettles her certainty. POV: Juniper. Beat: doubt creeping into hatred.

chapters.title: The Falsified Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo discovers eviction notices were backdated and tenant complaints fabricated by his boss, Voss, to fast-track demolition. POV: Theo. Beat: loyalty to employer cracking against conscience.

chapters.title: Letters Cross in the Night
chapters.summary: Both write their most vulnerable letters yet — hers about the stolen portfolio, his about the theft itself — and each realizes with dawning horror who the other must be. Beat: vertigo of recognition.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Theo comes to the café after hours; Juniper throws his own confession letter back at him. He doesn't deny it. POV alternates within the scene. Beat: raw, unresolved collision.

chapters.title: What Justice Isn't
chapters.summary: Juniper's neighbor Odile, facing illegal eviction, refuses to sue — she wants the truth aired, not damages. This reframes Juniper's fight: justice outside the law. POV: Juniper. Beat: moral deepening.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Theo copies the falsified ledgers, knowing it ends his career, and delivers them to Odile and Juniper — not as apology, he insists, but as duty. POV: Theo. Beat: costly integrity.

chapters.title: The Town Hall Reading
chapters.summary: At a packed council meeting, Odile reads the ledgers aloud; Voss stalls, then threatens litigation. The community land trust idea is born from the crowd. POV: Juniper. Beat: collective courage.

chapters.title: Half a Heart on Loan
chapters.summary: Juniper admits to Priya she's been loving Theo in installments — pieces, never the whole. A near-kiss in the kitchen is interrupted by a subpoena for Theo. POV: Juniper. Beat: longing interrupted.

chapters.title: Voss Strikes Back
chapters.summary: Voss exposes Theo's old plagiarism publicly to discredit him, weaponizing the very secret Juniper carries. Theo loses his job; the town wavers. POV: Theo. Beat: public shaming, private resolve.

chapters.title: The Songbook Page
chapters.summary: Juniper finds the songbook her late mother annotated — a margin note about forgiveness she'd never let herself read closely. She writes Theo one final letter, unsigned no longer. POV: Juniper. Beat: grief transmuted into choice.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Theo testifies before the county board, naming Voss and corroborating the forged records, sacrificing his career entirely. Juniper watches, cake flour still on her cuffs. POV: Theo. Beat: reckoning.

chapters.title: Whole Heart, Offered
chapters.summary: Outside the hearing, Juniper gives Theo her answer — not absolution but partnership: 'I don't lend pieces anymore.' They choose each other with eyes open. POV: Juniper. Beat: vulnerable, earned surrender.

chapters.title: The Trust Holds
chapters.summary: Resolution: the land trust vote passes; Voss faces investigation; the block is saved. Theo takes a job rebuilding rather than demolishing. POV alternates briefly. Beat: hard-won restoration.

chapters.title: Reopening Day
chapters.summary: The café reopens with a new name plate and Theo washing dishes without being asked. Old customers return; Odile cuts the ribbon. POV: Juniper. Beat: quiet joy, ordinary abundance.

chapters.title: Signed, Finally
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Juniper mails Theo a postcard across the counter — one sentence, signed with both their names. The last letter needs no anonymity. POV: Juniper. Beat: love in present tense at last.
